terra.problem: The sprinkle comparison doesn't match the idea of ascribing justice rather than mystery, so the joke doesn't connect.
The verse says God opens their ears in oppression, not that the hard place itself is the means by which He opens their ears.
The verse says God rescues the afflicted by their affliction; it doesn't say when the rescue happens.
Papa guesses what Minty would do now. He can remember his cookie cutter kids, but not guess what they would do or feel now.
The two bills comparison doesn't match the action in Elihu's warnings about being lured or led astray.
Papa claims to have watched a payday disappear into a car repair. Experiences outside his bakery must be described as things people do, not as his own.
The claim that giving is good in the Bible needs a reference outside this passage.
The claim that Job has many questions elsewhere in the book needs a reference.
Elihu describes the rain, but the text doesn't say people can't fully understand rain itself.
The joke compares Papa asking dough to rise with God's command to the rain, putting Papa in God's role.
The joke compares Papa's ability to cool a cookie rack with God's breath forming ice. Comparisons should stay on the human side.
The statement that God is patient needs a reference outside this passage.
Stamping an image of the sky onto a cookie isn't the same action as spreading out the skies, so the comparison doesn't fit.
The joke compares Papa's gold base with God's golden splendor, making the picture of God's majesty part of the joke.
The explanation turns 'wise in heart' into being wise in one's own estimation. That qualification isn't in the verse.
